subject: Information Theory
title: Interference
description: A short lesson to help you apply Interference.

hook.text: Your Wi-Fi slows down when the microwave runs. Both devices use the same 2.4 GHz band. They're fighting.

buildup.text: Interference is noise from other signals sharing the same channel. It's predictable but hard to eliminate.

discovery.text: Spread-spectrum techniques scatter signals across wide frequency bands, making interference much harder.

twist.text: Cell towers reuse frequencies at safe distances. Too close and they interfere. Too far and capacity drops.

climax.text: Managing interference is the central problem of wireless communication. Spectrum is shared, finite, and contested.

punchline.text: Other signals are noise. Your signal is their noise too.

quiz.question: Why does a microwave interfere with Wi-Fi?
options: Both use the same 2.4 GHz frequency band
